solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Primarily mumbled speaking?

indicators.note: primarily = first of all, so take the first letter

explanation.surface: A question about a way of talking that begins as a mumble.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: talk that opens with a mumble and carries on as speech is exactly the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An &lit: low, indistinct talk really is speaking in which mumbling comes first and foremost.

clue.text: Bother with problem climbing plant

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the letters read upwards

blocks.note: drat! and bother! are both mild curses
a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: A gardener annoyed by trouble with a climbing plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climbing plant' reads as one thing; 'climbing' is the instruction, turning DRAT + SUM upside down, and 'plant' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by class: the condiment comes from the seeds of a cabbage-family plant of the same name.

clue.text: Pundit snubbed new wave band

indicators.note: snubbed = cut short, like a snub nose, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: the New York group fronted by David Byrne; its last letter is cut

explanation.surface: A commentator refusing to acknowledge an up-and-coming group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snubbed' looks like the pundit being rude; it means cut short. Talking Heads lose their final S.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: television slang for a commentator shown only from the shoulders up, giving opinions.

clue.text: Local forgetting name boosted musical

indicators.note: forgetting the N leaves it out
in a down clue, boosted means pushed upwards, read bottom to top

blocks.note: a local is someone born there

explanation.surface: A resident who can't recall a title perks up at a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' looks like a pub, the usual crossword meaning; here it is a resident. NATIVE loses N, and ATIVE is read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Lloyd Webber and Rice show about Eva Perón.

clue.text: Remain popular, principally doing fine

indicators.note: principally = chiefly, first, so the first letter

explanation.surface: Advice on staying well liked while mostly doing well.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a literary verb, rare outside religious writing, which is why the wordplay is so plain.
explanation.definitionFit: Literary synonym: to dwell within, to abide, as the spirit is said to abide in a believer.

clue.text: Prisoner’s turning 44?

indicators.note: turning round, so the letters reverse

blocks.note: an old lag is a convict

explanation.surface: A convict changing into whatever answer 44 turns out to be.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cross-reference: 44 down is DAMSEL. The question mark flags that the answer is only an informal example of one.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: a young woman, the modern word for what 44 down calls her.

clue.text: One evening, around 6 — having cancelled 9 — enlightenment

indicators.note: the evening wraps around what follows
cancelling IX takes those letters out of SIX

blocks.note: nine in Roman numerals, cancelled from SIX

explanation.surface: A cryptic scheduling note that seems to point to other answers in the grid.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 and 9 look like cross-references to other clues; they are just numbers, one written as a word and one as a Roman numeral, so the subtraction leaves a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both mean a sudden clear understanding of something.

clue.text: Northern jerk, in principle, just the same

indicators.note: the northern jerk goes in the principle

explanation.surface: Calling a northerner an idiot on principle, all the same.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerk' tempts as an insult; it is a twitch, and the northern jerk goes in as one unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: exactly alike in every respect.

clue.text: Compiler in The Sun?

blocks.note: the sun goes down every evening, so it is one that sets

explanation.surface: Asking who writes the crossword in The Sun newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid, so the surface asks about its crossword writer; the second sense makes the sun itself the thing that sets.
explanation.definitionFit: Double definition: a crossword compiler, and whimsically anything that sets, as the sun does each evening.

clue.text: Pretend to search sewage?

blocks.note: search = go through; motions are, medically, bowel movements

explanation.surface: A sewer inspector only faking the job.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes 'motions' in its medical sense, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: doing something only for show, and literally rummaging through the sewage.

clue.text: Combinations of cards must be a dodgy hand at poker?

blocks.note: a count far too big: a pack holds only four of the next piece
the top cards in a poker hand

explanation.surface: A card sharp caught holding an impossible hand.
explanation.walkthrough: Ten aces would be a dodgy hand indeed. A tenace, in bridge and whist, is two high cards in one suit with a gap between, such as ace and queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Technical term: in bridge, a holding of two cards separated by one missing rank.

clue.text: Cleaned sheds quietly, and sulked

indicators.note: sheds = casts off, so a letter is lost

blocks.note: p = piano, quietly in music; one P is shed

explanation.surface: Someone who scrubbed out the garden sheds and felt sorry for themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sheds' looks like the thing cleaned; it is the verb, casting off one P.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both mean moping about in low spirits.

clue.text: Pulse raised over American — Hayworth, perhaps — getting cocktail

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means read upwards
in a down clue, over means placed above

blocks.note: gram is a pulse, as in chickpeas

explanation.surface: A heartbeat quickening over a Hollywood star as she orders a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulse' looks like a heartbeat but is the edible seed.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a tequila, lime and orange-liqueur drink served in a salt-rimmed glass.

clue.text: Start hoping Liberal makes hostile comment at last

indicators.note: liberal = free, loose, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Liberal's new optimism ending in a snipe at a rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' looks like the usual L for a party member; here it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a barbed remark made on leaving, from the Parthian archers who shot while retreating.

clue.text: Dirt from underneath my mannequin

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming from underneath means read upwards

explanation.surface: Finding grime under a shop-window figure.
explanation.walkthrough: Coming 'from underneath' only makes sense as an instruction in a down clue, where the letters climb from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a model figure used to display clothes.

clue.text: Second charming and mostly boring chap is hedonistic

indicators.note: mostly = most of it, so the last letter goes

explanation.surface: A second suitor, charming but rather dull, who lives only for pleasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second charming' reads as a description of a man; second is just S.
explanation.definitionFit: Near synonym: both describe someone who gives in to their own pleasures.

clue.text: Time machine that flies backwards — strange instrument

indicators.note: the flying machine is written backwards
rum is old slang for strange

blocks.note: a rum do is an odd business

explanation.surface: A time machine that travels in reverse, which would be a strange device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time machine' reads as a unit from science fiction; time is only T, and the machine is the flying one. Rum = strange is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by class: a drum pitched between the snare and the bass, used in marching bands.

clue.text: A contemptible person had to stir up trouble

explanation.surface: A nasty piece of work who set out to cause trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Had' looks like an auxiliary verb in 'had to'; it is the meal sense, ate. A git is British slang for an unpleasant person.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to campaign or stir people up for a cause.

clue.text: Aardvark can’t be arboreal for a stretch

indicators.note: a stretch of the text, running across word boundaries, holds the letters

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of can’t, through be, into the start of arboreal

explanation.surface: An aardvark can't live in the trees, not even for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is zoologically true: the animal digs burrows rather than climbing.
explanation.definitionFit: Alternative name: the South African animal is also called an earth pig or antbear, after its diet.

clue.text: Ailing businesses dig out good news, eventually

indicators.note: out = in disarray, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Struggling firms digging up something to celebrate at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dig out' reads as a phrasal verb; 'dig' is fodder and 'out' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: something unwelcome at first that turns out well in the end.

clue.text: Suspicious about sex aid

indicators.note: the word for suspicious goes about the other

explanation.surface: Being wary of a sex toy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sex aid' reads as one thing; sex is IT, and aid alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: help given freely to those in need.

clue.text: Like Italian to punch timekeeper’s hands-free kit

blocks.note: slang: I dig it = I like it
slang: to clock someone is to hit them

explanation.surface: An Italian who wants to hit the man with the stopwatch and his phone headset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hands-free kit' suggests a phone gadget; the joke is a timepiece without hands.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic definition: a clock showing numbers instead of hands is literally hands-free.

clue.text: Arranged to meet and test stone head, off and on

indicators.note: skip one letter, take one, skip one, take one

blocks.note: the abbreviation for the British weight of 14 pounds
h-E-a-D, the second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: Lovers who agree to meet, then test each other's resolve.
explanation.walkthrough: A tryst is a lovers' secret meeting; as a verb it means arranging one.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic verb: fixing a time and place for a rendezvous.

clue.text: Glam rock band vocalist blocked by Liberal politician, say, making false accusations

indicators.note: the vocalist is blocked by L sitting inside

blocks.note: British 1970s glam band, famous for 'Tiger Feet'

explanation.surface: A pop singer's career blocked by a politician spreading lies.
explanation.walkthrough: Mud were a British glam rock band of the 1970s. 'Liberal politician' reads as a unit, but the politician belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: slinging mud is making smears; 'say' marks a politician as just one example.

clue.text: Jockey possibly carrying unusual sign for spectator close to the action

indicators.note: the jockey carries the other letters inside
unusual = out of the normal order

explanation.surface: A jockey holding a strange placard for the crowd near the track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jockey' tempts as an anagram signal; here it is the rider, and 'unusual' does the mixing.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by description: someone seated beside the boxing ring.

clue.text: Periodically, driver steals fuel

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every other letter

explanation.surface: A motorist who now and then siphons petrol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Periodically' reads as how often the driver steals; it is the instruction to take every other letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: heavy oil burned in lorries and many cars.

clue.text: Compassion encapsulates English faith

indicators.note: to encapsulate is to enclose, so E goes inside

explanation.surface: Kindness containing a very English kind of belief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Encapsulates' is the verb doing the containing; the E goes one letter from the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Near synonym: religious devotion.

clue.text: Foretell welcoming a new preacher

indicators.note: the verb welcomes the letters inside

explanation.surface: A prophet who warns that a new preacher is coming.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a rare word from the Latin for preaching, used of Dutch Reformed ministers.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare synonym: a preaching minister or friar.

clue.text: He’s sinful, complex, and generous

indicators.note: complex = intricately put together, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A character sketch of a man who sins but is complicated and kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complex' reads as describing the man; it is the anagram signal. The fodder turns sinful into its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: putting others first.

clue.text: Discover Harry near hut

indicators.note: to harry is to harass, so the letters are knocked about

explanation.surface: Finding someone called Harry close to a shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like a man's name; it is the verb, to harass.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to find, especially by digging.

clue.text: Every individual jamming can debate etc.

indicators.note: every individual is jammed into the can

explanation.surface: Everyone cramming into a room to argue about everything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a verb; it is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by description: an informal session of lectures and debate on a topical issue.

clue.text: During riot, steal wheels before fight in storage area

indicators.note: to wheel round is to turn about, so the letters reverse

blocks.note: looting is stealing in the chaos of a riot

explanation.surface: Rioters making off with car wheels before a brawl in a warehouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wheels' reads as stolen car parts; it is the turning instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose definition: a box in which tools are stored.

clue.text: He backs end to receding layer of cells

indicators.note: backs = comes behind, so the He part goes last
receding = going back, so the letters reverse

blocks.note: He is the chemical symbol, expanded to the element's name

explanation.surface: A man putting an end to a thinning layer of cells.
explanation.walkthrough: He is read backwards from the usual abbreviation trick: the symbol gives the full name of the element, not the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: Technical term: the thin layer of cells lining blood vessels and the heart.

clue.text: Dog running for food

blocks.note: a machine that is on is running

explanation.surface: A dog chasing its dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running' reads as the dog's action; it means working, switched on.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by class: the meat of a mature sheep.

clue.text: Juvenile friends choose malts, shockingly

indicators.note: shockingly = in a shaken-up way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Underage friends shockingly picking whiskies.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a scandal: youngsters picking out malt whiskies.
explanation.definitionFit: Near synonym: friends made at school, so young ones.

clue.text: Twist nasty article in Die Zeit

blocks.note: a German definite article; Die Zeit is a German newspaper

explanation.surface: A spiteful slant given to a piece in a German newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' looks like a newspaper piece, which Die Zeit would print; it is the grammatical article, German for 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: Near synonym: a winding bend, as in a river.

clue.text: Old footballer is selected, yes?

blocks.note: a player who is selected is in the side

explanation.surface: A veteran player checking he has been picked for the team.
explanation.walkthrough: The inside right was an attacking position in the old five-forward football formation, now gone, hence 'Old'.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a player in a former football position.

clue.text: Short distance from home, stopping volatile host having argument

indicators.note: the home stops up the gap inside the host
volatile = unstable, so the letters are rearranged
having = with, so ROW is added

explanation.surface: A short-tempered host within walking distance, arguing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short distance from home' reads as one phrase; the definition stops at 'distance' and 'from' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: as far as a stone can be thrown, so very near.

clue.text: Stupid and innocent type showered after taking ecstasy

indicators.note: to take a drug is to take it in, so the innocent type holds the ecstasy inside
after = later in time, so in the written answer the showered part comes later

explanation.surface: A naive dimwit taking a drug and then a shower.
explanation.walkthrough: The ecstasy sits between the M and B of the innocent lamb; E for the drug is standard slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: slow-witted.

clue.text: Completely down with policeman arresting Republican

indicators.note: the policeman arrests R, holding it inside

blocks.note: to neck a drink is to down it

explanation.surface: A policeman arresting a Republican and knocking him fully down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down' reads as floored; it is the British slang verb to neck, to drink in one go.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: wholly, bodily, as when someone is thrown out neck and crop.

clue.text: Get rid of a book from Poland missing page

indicators.note: missing = lacking, so P is dropped

explanation.surface: Throwing out a Polish book with a page gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From Poland' means Polish, and losing P turns it into a word ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to do away with entirely.

clue.text: Enduring model: “I’ll be in bed, scratching head”

indicators.note: to model is to shape, so the letters are reshaped
scratching off its head, the first letter goes

blocks.note: BED without its first letter, also fodder

explanation.surface: A model's lazy promise to stay in bed, scratching her head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' looks like a person speaking; it is the command to reshape the letters that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Near synonym: impossible to remove, so lasting.

clue.text: One bad apple overwhelms Irish public service broadcaster, I think?

definitions.note: the definition is a phrase describing what the answer does

indicators.note: bad = spoilt, so the letters of one are rearranged
the apple overwhelms the broadcaster, swallowing it

blocks.note: Cox's Orange Pippin, a British eating apple
Raidió Teilifís Éireann, Ireland's national broadcaster

explanation.surface: A rotten apple spoiling Ireland's national broadcaster, in someone's opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One bad apple' reads as a proverb; 'bad' mixes ONE and the apple is a Cox. 'I think?' is not a hedge but the definition: the brain part where thinking happens.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic definition: the outer layer of the brain, where higher thought such as 'I think' takes place.

clue.text: Rank those people’s answer fills, not on TV

indicators.note: the answer fills the word for those people's, sitting inside it

explanation.surface: An order to rank people's answers to a quiz that has been taken off television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rank' looks like a verb for putting in order; it is the adjective, foul-smelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: no longer being broadcast.

clue.text: Whimsically remove my colour scheme

blocks.note: the prefix de- means remove, as in de-ice; 'whimsically' admits the liberty
my! and cor! are both British exclamations of surprise

explanation.surface: A mischievous instruction to get rid of the way a room has been painted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' looks like a possessive; it is the exclamation. The setter admits that taking remove as a prefix is a whimsical liberty.
explanation.definitionFit: Near synonym: a room's decorative scheme, colours included.

clue.text: Feel exhilarated or irate, and strange

indicators.note: strange = odd, out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A list of moods swinging from joy to anger to oddness.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a list of feelings, so 'strange' seems one more mood rather than the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to be so happy you seem to walk on air.

clue.text: Asians, mostly quiet, recalled embracing father

indicators.note: most of the word, so the last letter goes
called back, so the whole reads in reverse
the quiet word embraces father

explanation.surface: A group of Asians, mostly quiet, remembering how they held their father.
explanation.walkthrough: PA goes inside SILEN, and the whole, SILAPEN, is then read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by class: people from Nepal, a South Asian country.

clue.text: Radon for sale is silly, futile exercise

indicators.note: silly = scatterbrained, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Trying to sell a radioactive gas is a silly, pointless business.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is sound: radon is a radioactive gas no one would buy, so selling it really would be pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a task with no hope of success.

clue.text: Some visas in Estonia result in Scottish land transfers

indicators.note: some of the letters, so the answer is hidden inside

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of visas, through in, into the start of Estonia

explanation.surface: Visas granted in Estonia leading to property deals in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: A sasine is the Scots-law term for taking legal possession of land; the answer is a rare word, so the hidden word makes it gettable.
explanation.definitionFit: Regional legal term: in Scots law, the act of giving possession of land.

clue.text: Resentment, as underground cell gets diamonds for nationalists’ leader

indicators.note: the cell gets a new letter
for = in place of, so D replaces N

blocks.note: first letter of nationalists, coming out

explanation.surface: Nationalists' leader jailed underground, and resentful about the diamonds taken.
explanation.walkthrough: The swap works on DUNGEON's middle N; the first N in nationalists is what leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, mostly in the phrase 'in high dudgeon': angry resentment.

clue.text: Young woman checks middle of eyelid

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its centre, and with six letters that is the third and fourth

blocks.note: to dam is to hold back, check

explanation.surface: A young woman checking something in her eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Checks' looks like examining; it means holds back, as a dam checks water.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic synonym: a young unmarried woman, as in damsel in distress.

clue.text: Reveal properties for hire next to border

indicators.note: the two pieces sit side by side

blocks.note: in Britain a let is a property rented out
an edge, as of a cup

explanation.surface: A landlord disclosing rental properties near the frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a let is a rented property, so properties for hire are lets.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to reveal something by accident.

clue.text: Delicate predicament, having taken top off

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which comes off

blocks.note: a sorry state; its top letter goes

explanation.surface: A tricky situation made worse by someone removing their top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delicate predicament' reads as one phrase; the definition is only 'Delicate'.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: gentle, as in a light touch.

clue.text: Genus of lichens lives on plot

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after

blocks.note: to plot points is to graph them
to be is to live, exist

explanation.surface: A lichen growing on a patch of ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' looks like a patch of land, where lichen would live; it is a chart.
explanation.definitionFit: Technical term: script lichens, named for their writing-like markings.

clue.text: With two days to replace bishop, starts going back with bosses

indicators.note: going backwards, so the letters reverse
to replace is to take the place of, so the two days stand where the bishop was

explanation.surface: An office where two days off go to replace the bishop, and new starters answer to bosses.
explanation.walkthrough: DEBUTS reversed gives STUBED; DD then goes where the B was.
explanation.definitionFit: Near synonym: a boss is a round metal stud, so something studded has bosses.

clue.text: Regularly rush, though? Yes

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every other letter

explanation.surface: Someone asking whether to hurry and getting a casual yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' starts with the second letter here; the odd letters give nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: a murmur of agreement.

clue.text: Revolutionary’s rude, transfixed by reduced profit

indicators.note: the reduced profit is pierced by the rude word, which sits inside
cut short, so the last letter goes

explanation.surface: A rebel sneering while his dwindling profits are pinned down.
explanation.walkthrough: Giuseppe Garibaldi led the fight for Italian unification. The biscuit named after him is a British favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the 19th-century Italian revolutionary general.

clue.text: Start to suspect Mr Ed, say, is unrealistic candidate in election

indicators.note: the start of the word, its first letter

blocks.note: Mr Ed was the title animal of an American TV sitcom, who could speak

explanation.surface: Suspecting that a TV horse is standing for office without a hope.
explanation.walkthrough: A stalking horse stands in a leadership contest to test the waters for a stronger rival, with no real hope of winning.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a no-hope candidate put up to split the vote or test support.

clue.text: Virtually make up Chinese language

indicators.note: virtually = almost, so the last letter goes
in a down clue, up means read upwards

blocks.note: used as it stands, less its last letter

explanation.surface: Nearly inventing a language from China.
explanation.walkthrough: Kam, also called Dong, is a language of southern China.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by class: the tongue of the Kam or Dong minority people.

clue.text: Sweat damaged leather strap

explanation.surface: A strap of leather spoilt by perspiration.
explanation.walkthrough: A tawse is the Scottish schoolmaster's leather strap, used for punishment.

clue.text: Maybe McCartney and Starr’s final piece is outstanding

indicators.note: the final letter of Starr

explanation.surface: Paul McCartney and Ringo Starr's latest song is a triumph.

clue.text: Twisted young lady in Leeds, perhaps becoming half-hearted
